region: Lhasa, Gyantse, Shigatse and Everest north face
title: China — Tibet — Lhasa, Losar Pilgrims and Everest's North Face in February
subtitle: A permit-bound winter journey across the roof of the world, if the region is open
summary: A 13-day guided journey from Chengdu to Lhasa, Gyantse, Shigatse and Everest's north face in the cold season. The Tibet Autonomous Region often closes to foreigners in March and can close at short notice, so the plan targets February and depends on a permit that is not issued until weeks before travel.
introduction: Lhasa sits at 3,650 m, and in February the Jokhang and Barkhor fill with pilgrims after Losar. The group flies from Chengdu, spends three nights acclimatising in Lhasa among the Potala, Jokhang and Sera's debating courtyard, then drives west by private van with a guide over the 5,000 m Karo La to Gyantse's Kumbum and Shigatse's Tashilhunpo. A night at Shegar, at 4,300 m, precedes a midday visit to Everest's north face and Rongbuk Monastery, since the tent camps are closed in winter. The plan depends on a Tibet Travel Permit arranged by a licensed agency.

exceptional.vsOman: Oman was self-drive with tents and total independence. Tibet is the opposite: every day is on an approved itinerary with a guide, a driver and checkpoints, and nothing can be improvised. The reward is a living Tibetan Buddhist culture at 3,600 to 5,000 m rather than empty desert.
exceptional.vsPackageTourism: The route is the standard Lhasa to Everest circuit but run in February, when it is cold, quiet and shaped by Losar pilgrims rather than summer coach tours. It is not independent: the group can choose rhythm and rests but not the road.
exceptional.vsPortfolio: No other destination in the portfolio combines Tibetan Buddhist pilgrimage sites with a 5,000 m plateau drive and an Everest view, and none depends on a government permit that may be withheld for the whole of March. Ladakh (D41) offers a comparable culture and altitude with no permit gate, but is largely inaccessible in February.

duration.note: Day 1 outbound flight, day 13 return flight; 9 nights in the Tibet Autonomous Region plus 2 in Chengdu.

recommendedTravelWindow.rationale: The closure risk is the deciding factor. In 2024 and 2025 foreigners were barred for roughly 1 to 18/19 March, while February was open; 2026 reportedly had no closure (agency claim). The window starts after the main Spring Festival peak, after Losar (7 February) and ends before the March anniversaries. A 2019 closure of about 1 February to 1 March shows that February is not safe. March is the worst month: closed in recent typical years until about 20 March, with a thin late-March window of cold weather and snow at altitude.

februarySuitability.summary: Open in 2024 and, by agency reports, 2025 and 2026, but closures can be announced at short notice and permits stop without warning. If open, it is cold and clear with few visitors and Losar pilgrims; Base Camp tents are closed.

marchSuitability.summary: The usual closure period around Tibetan New Year and the 10, 14 and 16 March anniversaries (about 1 to 19 March in 2024 and 2025) makes March unreliable. The only likely window is after about 20 March, with cold nights, snow risk at passes and Base Camp tents still closed.

climate.regionNote: Approximate Lhasa climate normals (about 3,650 m); Everest Base Camp is much colder (February about -16 to 3 C per S12, nights about -15 C per S11). Figures are normals, not a 2027 forecast.

february.rainfall: Almost none; about 1 mm and 1 snowfall day across Tibet in February (S12).
february.notes: Strong sun and wind; Lhasa about 11 clear days; Shigatse nights to about -14 C; Base Camp -16 to 3 C.

march.rainfall: Dry, with occasional snow at altitude
march.notes: Warmer in Lhasa but passes can still have snow; March access is the issue, not temperature.

climate.snowAndMountainAccess: Roads to Namtso and Ngari can be blocked by snow (S12) and Namtso is frozen and not part of the plan. The Lhasa to Shigatse to Everest road is kept open and usually has little snow, but passes at 5,000 m can be icy. Base Camp tent hotels are closed from late October to mid-April (S11).
climate.seaConditions: Not relevant: no sea; Yamdrok Lake is partly frozen in February.
climate.airQuality: Good in Lhasa; Chengdu has winter smog.
climate.wildlifeSeasonality: Not a wildlife trip; yaks and Tibetan blue sheep may be seen from the road.

holidaysAndFestivals.name: Losar (Tibetan New Year)
holidaysAndFestivals.dates: Sunday 7 February 2027 (date set by Tibetan astrologers; local date may differ)
holidaysAndFestivals.impact: Shops and some sites close or reduce hours around the day; the Jokhang and Barkhor are very busy. Access restrictions have historically been tightened around Losar. The route starts after Losar.

holidaysAndFestivals.name: Spring Festival (Chinese New Year)
holidaysAndFestivals.dates: Saturday 6 February 2027; public holiday 5 to 13 February
holidaysAndFestivals.impact: Heavy domestic travel, high Lhasa hotel prices and tight Chengdu to Lhasa flights; the plan starts on 12 February to catch the end of the peak.

holidaysAndFestivals.name: Lantern Festival
holidaysAndFestivals.impact: Falls on the Everest day; little practical effect.

holidaysAndFestivals.name: Sensitive anniversaries
holidaysAndFestivals.impact: Historically linked to March closures; the plan ends well before them.

climate.ramadan2027: Not relevant: Tibet is predominantly Buddhist; Lhasa has a small Muslim community but no effect on the route.
climate.lunarNewYear2027: Saturday 6 February 2027; State Council holiday 5 to 13 February (S20). Losar is on 7 February. Travel from 12 February to avoid the peak, but fares and hotel rates remain elevated.
climate.tourismDemand: Low in winter outside the Spring Festival peak; hotels in Shegar and Rongbuk have limited capacity and heating.
climate.flightPriceSeasonality: Chengdu to Lhasa flights are cheapest in winter but spike around Spring Festival; Paris to Chengdu fares for February are typically above the lowest aggregator listing.

geography.summary: The southern Tibetan plateau at 3,600 to 5,250 m: the Yarlung Tsangpo valley, Yamdrok Lake, 5,000 m passes with glaciers, and the Himalayan crest at Everest.
geography.distinctive: Everest's north face seen from the Rongbuk valley at about 5,000 m, and a route that crosses three passes above 4,700 m in one week.

landscapes.description: Large turquoise lake at about 4,440 m below a pass of about 4,800 m, partly frozen in February.

landscapes.name: Lhasa and Yarlung Tsangpo valleys

culture.summary: Tibetan Buddhism as practised daily: pilgrims circling the Jokhang, monastic debate at Sera, working monasteries at Tashilhunpo and Gyantse, plus Losar customs in the days after 7 February.

culturalHighlights.name: Jokhang Temple and Barkhor kora
culturalHighlights.description: Seventh-century temple surrounded by a clockwise pilgrimage circuit used daily.

culturalHighlights.name: Potala Palace
culturalHighlights.description: Thirteen-storey palace, once the winter seat of the Dalai Lamas, with timed entry and closed Mondays.

culturalHighlights.name: Sera Monastery debate
culturalHighlights.description: Afternoon debating courtyard of Gelug monks; the schedule varies in winter.

culturalHighlights.name: Pelkor Chode and Kumbum, Gyantse
culturalHighlights.description: Nine-level stupa with dozens of chapels, built in the 1430s.

culturalHighlights.name: Tashilhunpo Monastery, Shigatse
culturalHighlights.description: Seat of the Panchen Lamas, with an active monastic community.

adventureHighlights.name: Karo La and Gyatso La passes
adventureHighlights.description: Two crossings above 5,000 m by van within three days; the main altitude exposure.

adventureHighlights.name: Everest north face day visit
adventureHighlights.description: A midday visit to Rongbuk and the Base Camp viewpoint at about 5,150 m in sub-zero cold; no overnight at Base Camp.

adventureHighlights.name: Barkhor and Lhasa old-town walking
adventureHighlights.description: Low-intensity walking at 3,650 m for acclimatisation.

signatureExperiences.title: Jokhang and the Barkhor with Losar pilgrims
signatureExperiences.description: Walk the clockwise kora around the Jokhang among pilgrims, see butter-lamp chapels and the roof, and take tea in an old-town teahouse.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: The group arrives days after Losar, when pilgrim numbers are high and tourists are few.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Agency guide; kora is free; Jokhang entrance by ticket and passport check; photography rules vary by chapel.
signatureExperiences.costNote: Entrance share; guide and van are in the day rate.

signatureExperiences.title: Potala Palace and Sera's debating courtyard
signatureExperiences.description: A timed hour inside the Potala followed by monks debating in the courtyard of Sera Monastery in the afternoon.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: Two living institutions of Tibetan Buddhism on one day; the debate is a rare public practice of monastic philosophy.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Agency books Potala tickets; debate hours vary and may pause in winter, so confirm with the guide.
signatureExperiences.costNote: Potala RMB 100 (about EUR 13) plus Sera entry (estimate).

signatureExperiences.title: Lhasa to Gyantse over Kampa La and Karo La
signatureExperiences.description: A day drive past Yamdrok Lake at 4,440 m and beside the Karo La glacier at 5,050 m, ending at the Kumbum stupa.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: One of the highest road crossings in Asia; the lake is partly frozen in February.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Private van with driver; Aliens' Travel Permit; no stops at checkpoints without the guide.

signatureExperiences.title: Everest's north face in winter
signatureExperiences.description: Overnight at Shegar (4,300 m), then a midday visit to Rongbuk Monastery and the Base Camp viewpoint with clear winter air.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: The north side is far less visited than Nepal's, and in winter nearly empty, with tent camps closed.
signatureExperiences.location: Shegar, Rongbuk and Everest Base Camp
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Aliens' Travel Permit via the agency; the guide checks road and weather; no overnight at Base Camp; Rongbuk guesthouse is basic.
signatureExperiences.costNote: Share of two vehicle days, guide, one hotel night and entrance (estimate).

travelStyle.summary: Agency-arranged guided tour in a private van with a driver and guide at all times; no independent movement is permitted in the TAR.

transport.summary: Fly Chengdu to Lhasa (the permit is checked at check-in), then private van with driver for the Lhasa to Shigatse to Everest circuit; the Qinghai–Tibet railway from Xining is a slower alternative.

modes.description: About 2 h 40 min; one-way fares about USD 220 to 330 (S10).
Xining to Lhasa 20 to 21.5 h, hard sleeper CNY 521 (S14); adds about two days and a Chengdu to Xining leg; same permit rules apply.

modes.mode: Private van with driver and guide
modes.description: Required for foreign visitors; fuel and vehicle in the price.

transport.carRental: Not available to foreign visitors in the TAR; self-drive is not allowed and all vehicles come with a driver through the licensed agency.

drivingRequirements.summary: Foreign travellers cannot drive or travel independently in the TAR; the agency supplies a van with a driver and an English-speaking guide.
drivingRequirements.internationalDrivingPermit: Not relevant: self-drive and rental are not possible for foreign visitors.
drivingRequirements.licenceNotes: Two of the four hold car licences, but this has no effect; none may ride a motorcycle or scooter and none needs to.
drivingRequirements.motorcycleNotes: Motorcycle hire is not available to foreign visitors in the TAR. Legal alternative: ride as passenger in the agency van.
drivingRequirements.recommendedApproach: Book a private van for four with a driver, an English-speaking guide, and fixed approved itinerary; confirm that the van has oxygen.

accommodation.summary: Pre-booked hotels and guesthouses approved for foreigners: Tibetan-style hotels in Lhasa, simple hotels in Gyantse, Shigatse and Shegar; Base Camp tents closed in winter.

camping.summary: Independent camping is not possible for foreigners on an agency tour in the TAR; tent camps at Base Camp are closed in winter.

physicalDifficulty.label: strenuous
physicalDifficulty.summary: Not technical, but every night is above 3,600 m, with two nights at 4,300 m, passes over 5,000 m and a day at 5,150 m in sub-zero temperatures. Altitude illness and the cold are the main hazards; nobody needs mountaineering skills.

itinerary.summary: Operational only if the TAR is open to foreigners in mid-February. The plan assumes a permit issued about 2 to 4 weeks before departure; if the permit is not issued or closure is announced, the whole route must be cancelled or moved. Two contingency days (days 2 and 12) absorb delays.

security.summary: No official advisory tells travellers to avoid the route, but the Tibet Autonomous Region is the one place in China where permits can be stopped without notice, tours are mandatory and surveillance is tight; the unresolved March (and possibly February) closure counts as an unresolved route restriction, so the status is conditional. Recent official alerts concern floods near the Nepal border, not the planned route.
security.assessedRoute: Chengdu; Lhasa; Lhasa to Gyantse via Yamdrok Lake, Kampa La and Karo La; Shigatse; Shegar; Rongbuk and Everest north-side Base Camp. Not assessed or visited: Gyirong, Ngari and Kailash, Namtso, Nyingchi, Chamdo and Tibetan areas outside the TAR.

regionalRestrictions: The TAR may be closed to foreign tourists with little notice; recent closures were about 1 to 18 March 2024 and 1 to 19 March 2025 and none in March 2026 (agency reports); no 2027 notice exists.
Tibet Travel Permit, Aliens' Travel Permit for Shigatse, Gyantse and the Everest region, only through a licensed agency; permits can be stopped without notice.
A guide must accompany foreign visitors throughout; independent travel, self-drive and camping are not possible.
Security checkpoints and surveillance; do not photograph police or soldiers, protests or sensitive sites; carry the passport and permit at all times.
Do not carry Tibet-related political material or letters or parcels from Tibetans; do not discuss the Dalai Lama's politics in public.
Kyirong (Gyirong) border and the Nepal road are closed after the August 2026 floods; this route does not use them.
Namtso and Ngari are frozen or snow-blocked in winter and are excluded; the Yarlung Tsangpo Grand Canyon and Chamdo are off-limits.
ordinaryRisks: Altitude sickness from the first night at 3,650 m, with two nights at 4,300 m and passes above 5,000 m; severe cases need rapid descent
Extreme cold and wind at Base Camp (to about -16 C)
Icy mountain roads and long drives
Limited medical care outside Lhasa and Shigatse; serious cases may need evacuation to Chengdu
Dry air, strong UV and dehydration
Landslides and floods linked to the 2026 monsoon event along the Nepal border
security.medicalAccess: Lhasa and Shigatse hospitals can treat altitude sickness and basic emergencies; serious cases are evacuated to Chengdu or abroad. The guide carries oxygen in the car; no reliable medical facilities exist at Shegar or Rongbuk.
security.insuranceConsiderations: Policy must cover altitude to 5,200 m, trekking/high altitude and medical evacuation, and must not exclude the Tibet Autonomous Region; a helicopter evacuation from remote Tibet can cost over USD 100,000 (S17).
security.reassessmentRequired: Re-check France Diplomatie, FCDO, Nederland Wereldwijd and the State Department before booking and two weeks before departure; triggers are any closure notice or refusal of permits, a closure around Losar or the March anniversaries, an extension or end of visa-free entry after 31 December 2026, new restrictions on the Everest region, or an advisory level change for Tibet.

practicalRequirements.visa: Conditional on nationality. French citizens are visa-free for up to 30 days until 31 December 2026 (S18); no extension announced as of 28 November 2026 (S19). If it lapses, a tourist visa is needed. A visa-free entry does not replace the Tibet Travel Permit; the 240-hour transit scheme does not cover Tibet (S08). Other nationalities must check with the Chinese embassy.
practicalRequirements.entry: Passport, Tibet Travel Permit (original, collected before boarding), police registration within 24 hours (hotels do it), arrival form; keep the passport and permit at hand for checkpoints.
practicalRequirements.passportValidity: At least six months after arrival and two blank pages (S03).
permits: Tibet Travel Permit (through a licensed agency only; 2 to 3 weeks, 3 to 4 weeks around Tibetan New Year)
Aliens' Travel Permit for Shigatse, Gyantse and the Everest region, arranged by the agency
Both are issued only if the TAR is open to foreigners
practicalRequirements.insurance: Altitude to 5,200 m, medical evacuation and legal assistance; verify that the TAR is not excluded.
practicalRequirements.connectivity: Google, WhatsApp, Instagram and YouTube are blocked; use a roaming eSIM and a licensed VPN set up before arrival; mobile coverage is poor away from Lhasa and Shigatse.
practicalRequirements.payments: Foreign cards can be linked to Alipay and WeChat Pay (D36 finding); carry cash for small guesthouses and monasteries.
practicalRequirements.medical: Discuss acetazolamide and altitude with a doctor before travel (S16); routine vaccines; bring prescribed medicines and a pulse oximeter.
practicalRequirements.fuel: Not relevant: the van and fuel are provided by the agency.
equipment: Down jacket rated to -20 C, thermal layers, hat, gloves, wind shell
Sun cream, lip balm and sunglasses for the UV at altitude
Sleeping-bag liner and power bank for cold rooms
Altitude medication and a pulse oximeter
Passport copies and Chinese-language hotel names
Offline maps and a translator app

advantages: Living Tibetan Buddhist culture at Jokhang, Sera and Tashilhunpo, close to Losar
Everest's north face in clear winter air with few visitors
No driving and no navigation: guide and driver handle everything
Winter is low season for hotels and sights
disadvantages: The region may be closed for much of the window and permits are issued only weeks before travel
Fully guided and fixed itinerary: no independence, no camping, no changing plans
Extreme cold and altitude, with nights above 3,600 m and passes above 5,000 m
Tight surveillance, checkpoints and a lack of freedom to discuss or photograph some topics
Expected cost above the group's EUR 2,500 limit
uncertainties: FIRST: The Tibet Autonomous Region has often been closed to foreign tourists for about the first three weeks of March (about 1 to 18 March 2024 and 1 to 19 March 2025; a longer closure of about 1 February to 1 March in 2019); it reportedly stayed open in March 2026, but the evidence is agency reports, not an official notice, and nothing is known for 2027. Closures can be announced with little notice. Permits cannot be confirmed before about 3 to 4 weeks before departure, so the whole trip may have to be cancelled late.
Visa-free entry for French citizens ends on 31 December 2026 with no announced extension; a visa may be needed and cost and processing time are unquantified.
No 2027 agency quotation for four people; the land cost is estimated and the realistic total is above EUR 2,500.
Altitude: the Everest night at 4,300 m after one week at 3,650 to 3,980 m is standard but not guaranteed to be safe; two travellers may fail to acclimatise and the Base Camp stop may be dropped.
Losar date in Lhasa may differ from 7 February, and monastery hours and the Sera debate schedule in winter are unconfirmed.
Insurance: many policies cap altitude or exclude the TAR; cover must be verified before booking.
